# Rulesha Glover-Payne

# Chief Human Resources Officer

![](/media/uploads/2026/10/Detroit_Public_Schools_logo-1.png)

Admits to the goal of hiring more teachers based on race.

- “One of the district’s goals is to recruit a more diverse workforce and we’ve been intentional with meeting this goal,” [Glover-Payne said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260516112728/https:/eastlansinginfo.news/elps-schools-statewide-struggle-to-build-diverse-teaching-staffs/). “Last year, I am happy to say that we made gains with hiring minority staff.”
- “I make it a point to attend college career fairs and most recently MSU just a few weeks ago,” [Glover-Payne said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260516112728/https:/eastlansinginfo.news/elps-schools-statewide-struggle-to-build-diverse-teaching-staffs/). “Only four students of color attended MSU’s career fair.”
- [Glover-Payne said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260516112728/https:/eastlansinginfo.news/elps-schools-statewide-struggle-to-build-diverse-teaching-staffs/), “Candidates that apply for a teaching position for ELPS, must submit a video cover letter and provide us with an equity statement.” She also said, “I have systematized the hiring process by creating a uniformed hiring process that hiring managers (principals, superintendent and directors) must follow.”
- [Glover-Payne admits](https://web.archive.org/web/20260516112728/https:/eastlansinginfo.news/elps-schools-statewide-struggle-to-build-diverse-teaching-staffs/): “I am currently working on procedures for hiring managers to utilize so they are identifying and interviewing more minority candidates, while at the same time ensuring that members of the interview committee reflect diversity.”
